Required evidence
Implement tests at the owning boundary and link results back to these IDs and FR/NF requirements: schema/value/reference validation; cross-tenant/branch allow/deny cases; publication/price retry and ordering; shared preview/player fixtures; offline/power/clock and region-fault scenarios; qualified media/rendering profiles; load traces; and observed user tasks. Any target the selected hardware cannot meet must be reported and explicitly revised or satisfied using a qualified profile, never silently weakened.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Governing controls and implementation boundary
text:
Governing controls and implementation boundary
**Decided requirements:** HTTPS, secure established authentication, server-side authorization and tenant isolation, separate device identities with revocable credentials, relevant audit, validated private media, recoverable backups, structured redacted telemetry and controlled updates. These are acceptance obligations; the foundation runtime alone does not implement tenant/device security.
Apply the inherited [authentication](../security/authentication.md), [authorization](../security/authorization.md), [data classification](../security/data-classification.md), [retention](../security/data-retention.md), [redaction](../security/telemetry-redaction.md), [secrets](../security/secrets-management.md), [production access](../security/production-access.md), and [error handling](../architecture/error-handling.md) policies. Do not invent cryptography, token schemes or password implementations. Accepted [ADR-0012](../adr/0012-verify-jwt-access-tokens-at-the-first-api-boundary.md) remains authoritative for human API access-token verification; Keycloak, server-managed sessions and scoped access are accepted under ADR-0024/ADR-0025 and the [identity/access policies](identity-and-access.md). PH-11 decision selection is complete; actual provider/session qualification remains PJ-24, and device-authentication design remains separate.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Actors and authorization
text:
Actors and authorization
The actor categories and capability allocation are **decided product policies** from the owner's 38 PH-11 answers. The [canonical identity policy](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix) owns the full matrix, custom profiles, scoped sharing, responsible-administrator approval, strong authentication, recovery/session limits and support rules. The first standard-role and tenant/branch access enforcement exists in the organizations module; [D-01 implementation status](tenant-data-design.md#implementation-status) and [D-02 implementation status](identity-session-design.md#implementation-status) distinguish verified capabilities from the remaining policy scope. Device identities, code-based pairing, revocation and erasure tracking exist on the server side per the [device enrollment design](device-enrollment-design.md#implementation-status); the Android player and its device-side enforcement remain PJ-12. Custom profiles cover only the organization and device capabilities that exist today; administrator approval requests and support access remain pending.
Platform operation has no default unrestricted customer-content access. Customer support needs explicit scoped, expiring consent with its real actor; no impersonation is selected. Player identities remain separate, restricted to their own authorized assignment/media/reports. Public company signup and automatic activation are selected, with completed PH-12 policy selection and PH-13/PH-15–PH-19 readiness gates; no existing company can be claimed by matching an email domain or name.
Check membership, tenant ownership, branch scope, operation and current resource state on the server. Cover detail/list/search/count/export, uploads/downloads/previews, manifests, synchronization reports and caches. Scope background work and reference validation as carefully as direct requests. Never trust a caller's tenant/role field or rely solely on a hidden button.
The first product slice needs both allow/deny tests with two companies and differently scoped branches, including resource-ID substitution, mixed-tenant references, stale membership, privilege escalation, unsafe assignment and bulk operations. The organizations suite covers its implemented company/branch operations; assignment, bulk and catalog cases arrive with their owning modules. Custom catalog fields, schema definitions, record/media bindings and imported layouts are subject to the same enforcement. [D-01](tenant-data-design.md) records implemented composite constraints and the approved decision to defer row-level security with compensating controls and reevaluation before real customer data.
Designated price saves automatically publish affected published content under completed PH-09. Server authorization must cover both the data mutation and its distribution targets; a draft-only edit permission cannot silently acquire publication power. Expose that consequence in the editing flow, keep unrelated drafts unpublished and audit actor/scope/revision/outcome. The [selected impact/approval rules](identity-and-access.md#publication-impact-and-delayed-work) reject an entire out-of-scope price mutation without partial publication or automatic approval fallback. Optional independent approvals distinguish a proposal from a saved effective price. Automatic work cannot bypass branch or tenant checks; technical verification remains pending.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Pairing and device lifecycle
text:
Pairing and device lifecycle
Pairing codes must be temporary, single-use, bound to the requesting device/enrollment intent, rate-limited and safe under concurrent claims; length/entropy/expiry are reviewed protocol decisions, not values invented in this plan. The claiming human must already be authorized for the destination company/branch. A displayed code is not an enduring device credential.
Use established platform protections for local credential storage, protected transport, rotation/revocation and controlled updates. Keep raw codes, tokens, signing material and credential-bearing links out of logs, public errors, screenshots and support bundles. Rooted/stolen or physically accessible devices are a separate exposure risk; offline playback cannot guarantee protection against a person who controls the hardware.
Revocation denies future server access; an unreachable device cannot receive an immediate wipe or new policy. [Selected release policies](release-policies.md#offline-authorization-and-clock-trust) and AT-15/AT-16 define the bounded authorization/clock behavior, distinct pending/confirmed erasure and verified cleanup/reset before another tenant's pairing. The device credential mechanism is selected in [ADR-0027](../adr/0027-propose-device-generated-credentials-and-code-based-enrollment.md); time estimation and hardware verification remain D-07. Do not claim instant remote erasure of cached data. No general remote shell or unattended support access is part of the release. [Commercial expiry/entitlement policies](commercial-policies.md#payment-expiry-cancellation-and-retention) add the known trial/paid/grace bound without exceeding AT-15, retroactive unreachable revocation or a bypass for suspended identities. Explicit limited commercial access is not security suspension.

The release does not require patient records, biometrics, card data, surveillance footage or other sensitive personal records. Configurable fields and a weekly-agenda view do not authorize collecting them; use public/synthetic events for examples and qualification. Prevent unsupported data collection and agree customer upload restrictions, purpose, retention/deletion/export, privacy notices, customer/operator responsibilities and incident handling under [PH-13](human-actions.md#ph-13). Catalog/layout imports and values are untrusted data. Validate type/size/reference/schema evolution and prevent arbitrary code, SQL, executable markup or implicit external fetches. Rendering text or selecting a typed reference must not expose private record/media access. Operational report/history defaults in the acceptance targets do not decide legal or security-audit retention.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Media and audit protections
text:
Media and audit protections
Validate type using trustworthy inspection as well as declared metadata; define size, dimensions, duration and supported codec/container bounds, safe names/paths and parser isolation. Arbitrary user uploads are not executable content. Malware/content inspection and processing tools are pending risk decisions; no unvalidated transcoding framework is selected. Download authorization must cover tenant/device/retained-publication access and prevent public object exposure.
Audit relevant membership/role changes, device pair/revoke/reassignment, publication and important media lifecycle operations with attributable actor, scope, target, time and outcome. Do not use sampled debug logs as the sole durable audit mechanism. Decide integrity, retention, authorized audit access and failure handling before implementing the affected actions. Expected failures have safe explicit errors; unexpected failures remain observable under the inherited error contract.

title: Teluni Security and Internationalization Requirements
heading: Internationalization
text:
Internationalization
**Decided:** engineering source/identifiers/docs remain English; interfaces must be designed for localization, initially `pt-BR` and `en-US`. Do not put user-interface copy inside domain rules or use translated labels as persisted identifiers. No i18n library is selected yet.
Separate message keys/parameters from display text, including validation, accessibility labels, device setup and operational states. Translate safely without permitting arbitrary executable markup.
Present dates, times and numeric values using the selected locale. User-facing server errors need stable codes and safe parameters rather than coupling business rules to localized sentences.
Explicitly model timezone per branch/device. PH-09 selected [calendar/DST behavior](release-policies.md#time-and-scheduling), device override then deliberately selected branch timezone and per-target local business time. Never inherit host timezone. D-06/D-10 implement matching preview/player fixtures and qualify trusted-time behavior against AT-16; business policy is no longer an unanswered PH-09 choice.
Locale is independent of timezone, currency and country. Monetary catalog fields use explicit currency and exact representation with scoped branch overrides; precision/rounding contracts must be reviewed before schema implementation. Formatting is not conversion; no automatic exchange service is selected. A generic catalog is not required to contain money fields.
Localize units and numeric presentation without changing persisted semantic meaning. Currency, decimal/grouping separators, longer translations and different date conventions must be tested.
Define the Android schedule/time interpretation with the same contract fixtures as backend preview. Changing UI language must not change actual publication timing or tenant permission.
The identity web module establishes this boundary with a typed pt-BR/en-US message catalog, Portuguese by default unless the browser prefers English, without selecting a library (D-10 remains open). Localization of the existing foundation shell and documentation portal is not performed.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
text:
Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
[Product architecture](architecture.md#pending-decisions) · [ADR-0018](../adr/0018-propose-tenant-owned-data-in-the-modular-backend.md) · [ADR-0025](../adr/0025-propose-application-owned-scoped-access-profiles.md) · [Identity and session design](identity-session-design.md) · [PH-20](human-actions.md#ph-20)

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Status and scope
text:
Status and scope
**Approved detailed design for D-01, 2026-10-18.** The owner approved it as proposed under [PH-20](human-actions.md#ph-20). It applies accepted ADR-0018 (shared database and schema, company as tenant, relational tenant constraints) and ADR-0025 (application-owned memberships and scoped grants) to concrete persistence and data-access rules, and records the row-level-security evaluation that ADR-0018 requires before the first product migration. The first organizations increment applies these rules; [implementation status](#implementation-status) distinguishes it from the remaining scope. Approval authorizes PJ-03 and the dependent modules to apply these rules; the human session mechanism is [D-02](identity-session-design.md).
The inherited [database principles](../database/principles.md), [authorization policy](../security/authorization.md), [transactions policy](../database/transactions-and-concurrency.md) and the selected [permission matrix](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix) still govern. Each module's implementation conventions will record its concrete tables, contracts and errors when the module is built; this document owns the rules every tenant-owned module shares.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Keys and relational constraints
text:
Keys and relational constraints
**Identifiers.** The backend generates an immutable random UUID for each row; it is the primary key and the public resource identifier, never authority. Clients cannot choose it.
**Tenant key.** Every tenant-owned table with its own `id` declares `UNIQUE (company_id, id)`. This is the only target that other tenant-owned rows may reference. Join tables and one-to-one extensions without an `id` (such as a grant's branch scope or a company's responsible administrator) cannot be referenced and need no tenant key, but their own references follow rule 3.
**Composite references.** Every reference from one tenant-owned row to another uses `FOREIGN KEY (company_id, <target>_id) REFERENCES <target> (company_id, id)`. A single-column foreign key into a tenant-owned table is prohibited. A mixed-company reference is therefore unrepresentable, independent of application predicates. An optional reference keeps the default `MATCH SIMPLE` semantics: a null target column means no reference, while `company_id` stays non-null.
**Immutable tenant.** The runtime role receives column-level `UPDATE` grants that exclude `company_id`, so no runtime statement can move a row between companies. Moving a device to another company is unlink plus new pairing (FR-02), never an ownership update.
**Tenant-scoped uniqueness.** Business keys such as branch names are unique within a company (for example `UNIQUE (company_id, lower(name))`, partial over non-archived rows where archival exists), never globally.
**Explicit referential actions.** Declare `ON DELETE RESTRICT` and `ON UPDATE RESTRICT` (Prisma `Restrict`) on every composite tenant reference. Prisma's implicit `SetNull` for optional relations would try to null the shared `company_id` and is never used on these relations. `CASCADE` is reserved for children inside one module whose lifecycle is genuinely owned by the parent, documented in that module's metadata.
**Cross-module references.** A downstream module may reference an upstream module's tenant key (for example future devices referencing `branches (company_id, id)`), following the module dependency direction. An upstream table never references a downstream one. Prisma requires a back-relation field on the referenced model; it is structural only, confers no read or write authority, and adapters never traverse it across a module boundary.
A structural test on the migrated database (catalog query, run with the integration suite) asserts rules 2, 3 and 4 for every table that has a `company_id` column. It fails when a new tenant table or foreign key omits the pattern, so the rule does not depend on review alone.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Request scope resolution
text:
Request scope resolution
Company-scoped operations carry the requested company in the path, for example `/companies/{companyId}/branches`. The path value is a request for a context, not proof of membership.
The session boundary ([D-02](identity-session-design.md)) supplies the verified principal and assurance.
The organizations capability resolves access with one current query joining the principal's active membership, the company's state and all unexpired grants in that company. It returns an opaque `CompanyAccess` value: company ID, membership ID, and each granted capability with its scope (whole company or an explicit branch set). Only the organizations capability can construct it.
No membership or a suspended membership returns `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` for the company path, without revealing that the company exists. Members of a suspended company receive an explicit company-state denial (code defined in PJ-03), kept distinct from limited commercial access under the [commercial policies](commercial-policies.md#payment-expiry-cancellation-and-retention). An in-scope actor missing a capability receives `PERMISSION_DENIED`. A resource outside the actor's scope is indistinguishable from an absent one (`RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`).
Access is resolved on every request from PostgreSQL without caching, so membership removal, suspension, grant reduction and expiry deny the next operation, within the 30-second bound selected in [P20](identity-and-access.md#ph-11-decision-record). Introducing a cache later requires a lifetime below that bound plus explicit invalidation, recorded here first.
Sensitive authority changes (membership status, administrator promotion or restoration, grant and profile edits, responsibility transfer) lock the company row first and then the involved membership rows in ID order (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`), and recheck the actor's current membership and administrator grant inside that transaction. Concurrent authority changes in one company therefore serialize instead of racing, and the fixed lock order avoids deadlocks. Every authority-changing writer must follow the same order.
Downstream modules receive `CompanyAccess`, ask it whether a capability applies to a branch, and obtain a branch filter (all branches or an explicit set) to put into SQL. They never accept a company, branch or role from the request body as authority.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Persistence adapter rules
text:
Persistence adapter rules
Every adapter operation on tenant-owned data takes the company scope from `CompanyAccess` as a mandatory parameter and uses it in every `WHERE`, `INSERT` and conditional `UPDATE`. Single-row lookups use the tenant key (`companyId_id` in Prisma), never a bare `id` lookup.
Branch filters and other authorization predicates are part of the query before pagination, counting and ordering. Nothing is loaded broadly and filtered afterwards.
A bulk request resolves its complete identifier set with the scope predicate in one query. If any element is absent or out of scope, the whole request fails as not found, with no partial effect.
Caller-supplied references (for example the branches of a grant) are validated by the composite foreign keys as the final guarantee. A tenant foreign-key violation maps to the module's not-found or validation error and never discloses whether the identifier exists in another company.
Cursors are bound to company, principal and list scope, and current predicates still apply on every page.
Deferred work and durable intents record company ID and the attributable actor; the executor resolves access again before any effect (IA-13). Workers that act as the system have their own explicitly reviewed capability.
Derived keys (caches, search entries, media object locations, manifests) include the company ID. A storage location never authorizes access; media access is checked against the owning row.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Row-level security evaluation
text:
Row-level security evaluation
ADR-0018 requires evaluating PostgreSQL row-level security (RLS) before relying on it or rejecting it. The evaluated mechanism was: enable RLS on each tenant-owned table with a policy such as `USING (company_id = current_setting('teluni.company_id', true)::uuid)`, keep the runtime role a non-owner (already true, because migrations own the tables), and set the tenant per transaction with `set_config('teluni.company_id', $1, true)`.
Concern
Finding
Mixed-tenant references
PostgreSQL performs foreign-key checks without applying RLS policies, so RLS alone does not prevent a row from referencing another company's identifier. Composite tenant keys are required either way
Connection pooling
The tenant setting is safe with the pooled Prisma/`pg` adapter only when transaction-local, so every tenant request must run inside an interactive transaction: extra `BEGIN`/`set_config`/`COMMIT` round trips and a pooled connection held for the whole callback
Principal-centric flows
Listing a principal's companies, accepting an invitation before a membership exists and public signup creating a company need extra policy keys or `SECURITY DEFINER` functions, enlarging the reviewed surface
Roles and migrations
The runtime role is not the owner, so policies apply without `FORCE`; the migration owner bypasses them for migrations/backfills. Integration tests already run as the runtime role, so policies would be exercised
Failure mode
A missing setting yields no rows, which fails closed
**Approved outcome: do not adopt RLS for the first slice.** The compensating controls are the composite tenant keys, immutable `company_id` grants, the mandatory scope parameter, per-request access resolution, the structural catalog test and the two-company adversarial suite below. **Reevaluate before PJ-14 admits real customer data or public signup**, when a second database consumer (worker, report or raw SQL path) appears, or immediately after any cross-tenant defect. Adapters already receive the scope, so adopting RLS later needs a new ADR, policy migrations and a transaction-local context in adapters, not contract changes.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Platform and administrative scope
text:
Platform and administrative scope
Platform administration is a separate capability held by individually provisioned platform accounts (P11), not a company membership and not a bypass of tenant predicates. The first slice exposes no platform routes. When added, platform operations may manage company lifecycle and commercial metadata; customer content requires an explicit, expiring, company-authorized support grant (P33/P34, IA-14) stored as tenant-owned data. Database, migration and backup access are operational access under [production access](../security/production-access.md), never product authorization.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Organization audit in the first slice
text:
Organization audit in the first slice
The organizations capability owns an append-only, tenant-owned audit table. Each membership, invitation, grant, profile, responsibility and company-setting change writes its event in the same transaction as the change, so a failed change leaves no event and a committed change exactly one. The runtime role receives only `INSERT` and `SELECT` on it, which makes rows immutable through the application. Events record actor principal and membership, action, target type and ID, outcome and allowlisted details, never secrets or full payloads. Branch events include the branch name at the time of the event, so later renames or name reuse do not relabel past changes; older events without that detail remain readable. Each event also records the branches it concerns (a branch change names its branch; a branch-scoped grant or invitation names its branches) in an append-only join table; an event without branches is a company-level operation. Company administrators read company scope; branch managers read only events that concern at least one branch and only branches they manage, so company-level events and operations that also reach other branches stay hidden. Retention, IP metadata and cross-module audit integrity remain [D-09](architecture.md#pending-decisions) and [PH-13](human-actions.md#ph-13); no deletion job is introduced.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Required verification
text:
Required verification
Every tenant-owned module reuses one synthetic two-company fixture: company A with branches A1 and A2, company B with branch B1, and principals for A's administrator, an A1 manager, an A1 operator, B's administrator, a principal holding memberships in both companies with different scopes, and an outsider. The first slice must show, against real migrated PostgreSQL:
Substituting another company's or branch's identifier in path, query or body returns not found, and lists, counts and cursors never include out-of-scope rows.
A direct runtime-role `INSERT` of a mixed-company reference fails with a foreign-key violation, and a runtime `UPDATE` of `company_id` is denied by privileges.
Membership removal or suspension and grant expiry deny the next request; no cached access survives.
A branch-restricted manager cannot act on another branch, and a bulk request containing one out-of-scope identifier is rejected entirely.
The multi-company principal sees only the requested company's data, and switching company relies only on the path plus current membership.
The structural catalog test passes for every tenant table and foreign key.
A failed authority change leaves no audit event; a committed one leaves exactly one, readable only within scope.

title: Teluni Tenant Data Ownership and Access Design
heading: Implementation status
text:
Implementation status
The [`organizations` API module](../../apps/api/src/features/organizations/module.ts) owns companies, branches, memberships, standard-role grants and branch scopes, creator responsibility and append-only audit. Its [Prisma schema](../../apps/api/prisma/schema/organizations.prisma), [reviewed migration](../../apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261018010000_organizations/migration.sql), semantic metadata and runtime grants implement composite tenant references and immutable tenant columns. Company creation atomically creates the creator's membership, responsibility and administrator grant with one audit event; it confers no commercial entitlement. Creation retries compare an immutable fingerprint of the original normalized inputs, so later company-setting edits do not change the idempotency decision. Company and branch updates use expected versions; stale-write classification stays on the transaction connection. Access resolves current membership, company state and effective grants on every request; administrator/manager grants require strong authentication.
The [two-company integration suite](../../apps/api/test/organizations/integration.test.ts) exercises tenant/branch isolation, additive scopes, current revocation/expiry/suspension, idempotency, stale versions, name uniqueness, atomic audit, grant and transfer rules, runtime privileges and migrated schema structure. Branch and audit cursors are validated and bound to company, principal and collection; branch cursors also bind the effective branch scope. The [web module](../../apps/web/src/organizations/routes.tsx) uses the generated SDK for company creation/listing, step-up recovery and branch creation/rename/archive with pt-BR/en-US copy. [Browser journeys](../../apps/web/test/e2e/organizations/companies.spec.ts) exercise real login and OTP enrollment.
Company lists use keyset pagination by immutable creation time and ID, newest first, with 50 entries by default and at most 100 per page. Cursors bind the principal and collection; active-membership and effective-role predicates run again before each page. Renaming a company does not move its page boundary. Lists are live rather than snapshots: new companies appear on a restarted first page, and removed/suspended memberships disappear immediately. The web panel preserves company cursors in the URL and provides capability-gated settings and change-history views. Settings capture the edited version and require review after a conflict or unknown write outcome; the history translates allowlisted actions/field names and distinguishes the current actor from another member without exposing raw payloads. Member administration lists memberships with presentation names and emails taken from each person's last verified sign-in (identity's presentation port, called only with principal IDs from the authorized page), never as authority or account-linking evidence.
Strongly authenticated company administrators can page through the company's memberships and suspend, reactivate or remove (terminally, in this company only) a membership with its observed version, each with one audit event. The responsible administrator cannot be suspended or removed, the last active administrator is protected, and reactivating an administrator requires the responsible administrator with strong authentication no older than five minutes (P10/P14). An unchanged status is a no-op. The panel confirms each change with the version observed when it was requested, reloads after a conflict or unknown outcome before another change, and offers recent re-authentication when restoring an administrator.
Strongly authenticated company administrators also grant and revoke standard roles (the [roles and responsibility transfer migration](../../apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261018030000_roles_and_responsibility_transfer/migration.sql) adds the transfer table and the runtime grants these writes need). A grant names a role and either the whole company or one to 100 explicit active branches of that company; company administration is always company-wide. Unknown, archived and other companies' branches are rejected alike as invalid input, and a new branch never joins an existing branch grant. An optional expiry must be at least a minute in the future and is never renewed (P30); an identical effective grant is returned instead of duplicated. Roles change by adding and revoking grants; revocation is terminal for that grant, a revoked or expired grant is a no-op, and grants are never edited in place. Only the responsible administrator, with strong authentication no older than five minutes, grants company administration: that action is the P10 approval, and no request-and-approve queue exists for proposals from other administrators. Revoking keeps the responsible administrator's and the last active administrator's company administration. Each grant change writes one audit event with its role, scope and branch count.
Responsibility moves only through a transfer that the responsible administrator proposes to another active company administrator, with strong authentication no older than five minutes, and that the successor accepts, also with five-minute strong authentication, while still an active administrator and while the proposer is still responsible. A company has at most one pending transfer (a partial unique index); a proposal can be accepted for seven days, an engineering choice that mirrors invitation validity. The proposer can cancel and the successor can decline it; an expired proposal stays closed and is marked expired when the next one is made. Only the two parties see a pending transfer, in the company detail with the counterpart's presentation name; every other member, including other administrators, receives not found for it. Proposal, acceptance, cancellation and decline each write one audit event, and acceptance updates the company's responsibility row under the company lock. The former responsible administrator stays an ordinary administrator, which the new responsible administrator can then suspend or remove. The panel lists each member's effective grants with their branches and expiry, adds a grant through a role, scope, branch and optional expiry form (the administration choice appears only to the responsible administrator), confirms each revocation, proposes a transfer from an active administrator's row, and shows the pending transfer to its two parties with accept, decline or cancel and recent re-authentication when the API asks for it.
Branch-scoped audit reads follow the [branch audit scope migration](../../apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261019020000_branch_audit_scope/migration.sql), which adds `organization_audit_event_branches` with composite references to the event and the branch, grants the runtime role only `INSERT` and `SELECT`, and backfills existing events from immutable sources (branch event targets and the branch scopes of grants and invitations). The branch predicate is part of the audit query before ordering and the limit, and audit cursors bind the caller's branch scope. Strongly authenticated branch managers open the panel's change history, which then describes it as the history of the branches they manage; operators still have no audit access.
Company-customized access profiles follow the [access profiles migration](../../apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261019030000_access_profiles/migration.sql), which adds the tenant-owned `access_profiles` table and lets a grant carry exactly one of a standard role or a composite reference to a profile of the same company (a `CHECK` enforces it). A profile is a company-unique active name plus one to five delegable capabilities: viewing branches, managing invitations, viewing the audit history, viewing screens and pairing/managing screens (the matrix's "additional grant" for operators). Company administration, settings, branch and member management are never delegable, so a profile can neither bypass the responsible administrator's P10 approval nor confer authority its grantor lacks. Every profile also includes basic company visibility. Assurance follows each capability rather than the label: managing invitations, reading audit and managing screens require strong authentication of every holder, while viewing branches and screens works in a standard session, so renaming or recombining a profile never lowers an assurance requirement. Profile grants use the same scopes, expiry, identity rule and revocation as role grants, and branch-scoped invitation and audit reach work exactly as for branch managers. Access resolves the profile's current capabilities on every request and ignores archived profiles, so an edit reaches every holder on the next request. Strongly authenticated administrators list, create, rename, recombine and archive profiles with expected versions under the company lock; a company keeps at most 50 active profiles, and a profile with effective grants cannot be archived. The profile detail lists current holders with their scopes and branches (up to 500) before an edit, and each create, edit and archive writes one audit event; edits record added and removed capabilities and the number of affected grants. The panel's Access profiles view lists profiles with their usage, creates and edits them, shows the holders and asks for confirmation before a capability change that reaches members, and the member grant form offers active profiles beside the standard roles. Invitations still offer only standard roles, and profiles will gain capabilities only as the modules that own them are built.
Company invitations, including branch managers inviting operators to their own branches, follow the approved D-13 [invitation and email delivery design](invitation-delivery-design.md#implementation-status); a removed membership now stays as history, and one current membership per principal and company is a partial unique index. Support access and bulk operations are not implemented. Their rules above remain requirements; fixture SQL used to test alternate memberships is not a product administration flow. RLS reevaluation remains due before real customer data under PJ-14. Validation evidence and incomplete work remain in [PJ-03/PJ-24](implementation-plan.md#current-work).
These cases implement the tenant portion of [IA-03](identity-and-access.md#required-verification-cases), IA-08 and IA-10 and the NF-01 boundary. They do not replace the identity, session and assurance cases owned by D-02 and PJ-24.
